questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Easy through the website flatmates which is very popular in Australia

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living off campus might be a lot cheaper than living on campus, and you can still live very close to campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Housing through uni was extremely expensive, even compared to living prices in copenhagen

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Not much registration, you choose courses before getting there and that was it.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Different centers where you could ask for help. Otherwise you could always email professors, they were very helpful as well.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all of the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took two 1st year level courses and two 3rd year level courses. I would say the levels made sense, as 1st year courses were introductory and you needed no knowledge before starting, and a certain level of knowledge was required for the 3rd year courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different. There was a lot of memorizing and quizzes and mid-semester-tests, but that took some of the pressure of the last exams.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Australia in the wine world (1st year level)
Foundations of computing (1st year level)
Drugs: From discovery to market (3rd year level)
Drugs affecting the nervous system (3rd year level)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Any that fits your interests. Especially 1st year level courses should be fine even if you know nothing about it in the beginning. Professors are very aware that it is the first year of uni for many students in these courses, and they make sure to explain everything.
